title: canary-rollout-scratchpad-samir-patel
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for the upcoming canary rollout of model serving runtime v2.3. This is NOT the canonical runbook — sync with release-engineering doc and PMs before execution. Notes, commands, and immediate TODOs are here for the engineering on-call to reuse.

Context:
- Release: serving-runtime v2.3 (performance improvements, KV cache fix, small optimizer change).
- Target model configured in prod: model-redwood/llama-compat:v1.4.2-quant (pinned in route config).
- Canary window requested by product: 3 days, starting 2026-03-05 00:00 UTC (overnight low-traffic start).
- Primary goal: validate latency P95 and error rate under production traffic and spot any regressions vs v2.2 baseline.

High-level plan (quick):
1) Pre-checks (T-24h): ensure canary infra ready, dashboard graphs baseline, smoke tests green.
2) Push canary to 5% traffic for 2h; monitor metrics + logs.
3) If healthy, increase to 20% for 4h.
4) If still healthy, 50% for 6h.
5) If healthy at 50% and no critical signals for 12h, promote to 100% or schedule full rollout.

Canary checklist (detailed):
- [ ] Finalize rollout config in redwoodctl and commit to infra repo (branch: release/v2.3-canary).
- [ ] Confirm model pins in route config: route: "gen-text-prod" -> model: "model-redwood/llama-compat:v1.4.2-quant" (fallback: "model-redwood/llama-compat:v1.4.1-cpu").
- [ ] Create canary release PR: link in linked_artifacts (PR #4521).
- [ ] Run static preflight: config lint, infra plan (terraform plan), secrets check.
- [ ] Notify stakeholders: #release-ops, CS on-call, SREs. Scheduled email to app owners.
- [ ] Tagging: add release notes draft in Confluence (link above).

Smoke tests (must pass before moving to 5%):
- 10 synthetic generation requests at varying prompt lengths (10/50/200 tokens) succeed with no increases in error codes vs baseline.
- Embedding flow smoke (if shared model): 5 embedding requests.
- KV cache warmup test: repeat prefix requests and validate token generation latency decreases by >5% after warmup.
- Sanity: sample of function-calling flows (if enabled) return expected JSON schema.

Key metrics & thresholds (automatic alerts / manual gates):
- Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% absolute increase over baseline -> immediate rollback.
- Client-level 4xx spike? Investigate (rate limit or client bug), don't auto-roll back unless correlated with code change.
- Latency P95 increase > 30% over baseline for consistent 30+ minutes -> pause and investigate.
- Token generation throughput drop > 40% -> investigate CPU/GPU saturation.
- GPU memory OOMs observed -> immediate rollback.
- Cost anomaly (unexplained >20% increase) -> notify infra-finance and investigate.

Rollout commands (reference):
- Create canary: redwoodctl rollout create --name v2.3-canary --route gen-text-prod --model model-redwood/llama-compat:v1.4.2-quant --traffic 5
- Update traffic: redwoodctl rollout update v2.3-canary --traffic 20
- Promote: redwoodctl rollout promote v2.3-canary (promotes to 100% and updates route pin in infra repo)
- Rollback: redwoodctl rollout rollback v2.3-canary --to-version model-redwood/llama-compat:v1.4.1-cpu 
- Quick kill (emergency): redwoodctl rollout abort v2.3-canary --force
- Infra check: terraform -chdir=infra/prod plan 

Observability & dashboards to watch (links in Confluence release page):
- Per-route latency: gen-text-prod p50/p95/p99 (compare to baseline tag v2.2).
- Error rate: 5xx by route and by handler (tokenizer, runtime, network).
- Hardware metrics: GPU mem, GPU utilization, host CPU, network egress.
- Cost telemetry: token cost / minute, GPU-hours.
- Traces: sample traces for slow requests, look for kernel retries or serialization stalls.

Rollback & incident playbook (short):
- If threshold breached: 1) Pause rollout (set traffic to previous safe % or 0). 2) Rollback to pinned fallback model (v1.4.1-cpu) or previous runtime (v2.2). 3) Open incident on PagerDuty and notify release channel. 4) Collect traces/logs and create a hotfix branch if required.

Version pinning notes:
- Route-level pin should be committed to infra repo after full rollout. For canary, use explicit canary config (not the global pin).
- Keep fallback model tag immutable (do not auto-upgrade fallback).
- Document in Confluence which consumers rely on the route (apps, internal teams).

Testing matrix to run during canary:
- Functional QA: small prompt set (10 prompts) from product evaluation suite.
- Regression eval: run eval harness against golden set (metrics: ROUGE/BLEU not relevant; for generation we rely on rough heuristics + semantic similarity) — compare top-k perplexity and output quality samples.
- Load test: ramped synthetic load to 50% of normal peak to validate throughput scaling path (use separate load cluster, not production traffic).

Open questions / unknowns (TODOs):
- [ ] Does dedicated capacity customers get routed to canary? (should be NO; confirm routing policy). Action: check smart-routing policy PR.
- [ ] Are there any downstream cache invalidation effects for cached prompts? Confirm with privacy/cache team.
- [ ] Confirm retention window of structured logs for 7 days for snapshotting runs.

Post-mortem / follow-up actions (if all good):
- Finalize release notes and call out regression check results.
- Update model pin in infra repo and remove canary flag.
- Add a short blameless postmortem if any incidents occurred.

Quick snippets (copy-paste):
- Can create canary (5%):
  redwoodctl rollout create --name v2.3-canary --route gen-text-prod --model model-redwood/llama-compat:v1.4.2-quant --traffic 5

- Rollback to fallback model:
  redwoodctl rollout rollback v2.3-canary --to-version model-redwood/llama-compat:v1.4.1-cpu

Notes to self: keep the early window small and staffed (first 4 hours needs active monitor from SRE + oncall release eng). If any ambiguous signal, pause increase and open a thread with the subsystem owners (runtime, infra, model team).

End of scratchpad.
